title: Console: Guided routing policy templates + scenario sandbox
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a set of curated routing policy templates and a scenario-driven sandbox in the Console to help customers create region/tier/fallback policies quickly. Templates will be opinionated starting points (latency-first, cost-first, region-preferred, cold-fallback) and the sandbox will let users run synthetic preview traffic across regions/tiers and visualize model variant fallbacks and cost/latency projections.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI exposes 6 initial templates with editable parameters: latency-priority, cost-priority, region-first, tiered-fallback, availability-optimized, and blue/green-ready
Users can open a template into the policy editor, modify rules, and save as a tenant policy or draft

Scenario sandbox accepts a JSON input or guided wizard to produce 3 synthetic traffic mixes and visualizes per-region latency distribution, expected token-cost delta, and fallback events over a 60s simulated window
Validation runs on save and surfaces errors/warnings: incompatible model variant mapping, unreachable route conditions, circular fallbacks
Preview provides a side-by-side diff for the current live policy vs. the drafted template and highlights customer-visible behavioral changes
Export/import of policy templates in JSON format is supported with schema versioning and compatibility checks
Telemetry events emitted for template usage and sandbox simulations for measurement (sampled)
notes: Rationale: customers repeatedly ask for 'starter' policies and a safe way to reason about fallbacks without creating incidents
Design brief attached — focus on low-friction onboarding for platform teams and product engineers
We want templates to be editable; avoid locking customers into opaque black-box rules
Keep template logic compatible with both Hosted and Dedicated deployments — refer to routing capability matrix in engineering doc
Sandbox should be able to run quickly in-browser for small simulations; larger simulations can be proxied to backend job runner
